newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan tunes in to foreign-made TVs.
newsitem.headline: Japan tunes in to foreign-made TVs.

text.p: Japan, which built up a powerhouse reputation in the 1970s by conquering the electronics world, is now itself falling victim to television imports.
Industry data released on Tuesday showed that for the first time Japan imported more TV sets last year than it rolled out of its domestic factories.
Imports rose slightly to a record 7.51 million sets while domestically produced sets fell a sharp 17.5 percent to 6.48 million, the Electronic Industries Association of Japan said.
Malaysia topped the list of television exporters to Japan with 2.41 million units, followed by Thailand with 1.59 million sets, the association said.

But the change does not mean that Japanese brands are necessarily losing their favour among consumers. Many of the imports come from Japanese companies that have moved production offshore to avoid high labour costs and the high yen.
An industry spokesman said the strong value of the yen combined with a drive to manufacture sets where the market is located had contributed to the shift.
The figures also show that videocassette recorder production is heading the same way.
VCR output in Japan in 1996 was down 21.1 percent from the previous year to 9.98 million units, with imports exceeding exports for the first time ever.
